scope: R0 mirror-vs-official byte comparison for every environment type that has both sources, plus verification of publisher checksum files for the four assets previously recorded as having none
status: mirror-comparison-complete; publisher checksums adopted for Rust and PHP, documented as unusable for Maven and ADB

network.note: All downloads went to a temporary directory. No installer ran, nothing was extracted into the managed root, and no workspace file outside src-tauri/src and docs was written by the comparison itself.

mirrorComparison.method: Download the same version from the official URL and the mirror URL used by SOURCE_MIRROR, then compare SHA-256 of the complete file.

results.note: The Tsinghua mirror only carries majors 25/21/17/11/8, matching jdk_tuna(); the audited official JDK 27 asset has no mirror counterpart to compare.

publisherChecksums.method: Locate a publisher-published checksum file, read its value, and recompute the matching digest over the previously downloaded official asset.

results.reason: The download verifier only accepts SHA-256; the row now states that Apache offers SHA-512, so the asset is explicitly unverified rather than undocumented.
Google publishes only SHA-1 in its SDK repository index; verifying a weaker digest would overstate assurance. The row states the reason instead.

defectsFixed: download_spec_with_verification unconditionally overwrote every branch's verification and expected_size, so any per-branch decision (or the caller's digest) was discarded; a branch that decided now keeps its decision.
Rust's official branch hard-coded VerificationInfo::default(), discarding the publisher checksum even when resolved.
Rust's mirror branch would have inherited the official digest; it now states that the mirror copy was not proven byte-identical.
adoptedSources: parse_php_releases attaches windows.php.net/downloads/releases/sha256sum.txt with the exact archive filename
explicitUnverifiedReasons: Maven rows: Apache only publishes SHA-512
ADB rows: Google only publishes SHA-1
codeChanges.newConstant: VerificationInfo::DEFAULT_UNVERIFIED_REASON distinguishes an untouched default from a deliberate unverified decision.

notVerified: Mirror behaviour over time: a mirror can diverge after this audit; the comparison is a snapshot, not a guarantee.
No mirror download was executed through the application's own download path, only through direct HTTP fetches.
Windows VM installation remains unverified, so R0 cannot be closed.
limitations: The JDK comparison used major 25 because the mirror does not carry major 27.
Comparing official and mirror bytes proves they agree now, not that either is authentic; publisher checksums remain the authenticity anchor.
Maven and ADB stay unverified by design until the verifier supports SHA-512 and a deliberate decision about SHA-1 is recorded.
